text:
This looks like autumn 2009. Unemployment is 9.7% and headline CPI is -1.44% YoY, which fits the trough in inflation around July–October 2009. The fed funds rate is 0.11%.

Unemployment first reached 9.7% in August 2009 (it was 9.6% in August and 9.8% in September, per the vintage data). The 3-month average of payroll changes is -318k, which also fits an earlier, deeper-loss period. Industrial production is -10.7% YoY, consistent with mid-2009; it was about -10.9% in July and -10.7% in August.

Headline CPI was -1.5% in July 2009, -1.4% in August, and -1.3% in September. Core CPI at 1.46% looks like August 2009 (1.4%). The 10-year yield at 3.31% fits August 2009 (about 3.5%) or September (about 3.3%). The 6-month equity return of 31.6% fits a window beginning in March 2009 and ending in August or September. The 12-month equity return of -6.6% fits September 2009, since the figure for August 2009 would be about -10%. The VIX at 25.19 also fits September 2009, when it was around 25.

Given the data, I'll go with September 2009.
